title: Best Beaches & Beachfront Apartments Stari Grad 2027
metaDescription: Stari Grad beaches on Hvar: Banj, Lanterna and sandy Maslinica, with distances, where to stay near the water and practical tips for 2027.
content:
## Best Beaches in Stari Grad

Stari Grad sits at the end of a long, sheltered bay on the north-west coast of Hvar. Small pebble coves and concrete bathing platforms line both sides of the harbour. Most are a 5-10 minute walk from the old town. Sea temperatures reach about 26°C in summer.

### Banj Beach
Banj is a pebble bay on the north side of the bay, about 500 m from the centre. It has sunbeds for hire, showers, changing rooms and a restaurant. Access is step-free, so it suits wheelchair users and very young children. The water is shallow and calm. It is the easiest option for anyone with a stroller.

### Lanterna Beach
Lanterna lies on the south side of the bay, about 800 m from the centre. The walk along the waterfront promenade takes roughly 15 minutes. It has a small shingle beach, flat rock platforms with steps into the sea, showers, changing rooms, sunbeds and a restaurant. From mid-July to mid-August the sun sets directly into the sea in front of the platforms. Evening is the best time to come.

### Maslinica Bay
Maslinica is 2 km from the centre and is one of the few sandy beaches on Hvar. A maintained coastal path leads there on foot or by bike, and there is also road access with parking nearby. The beach is mostly shade-free. Bring an umbrella. It is the best choice for families with small children who want sand rather than pebbles. The five-star Maslina Resort now fronts part of the bay, so check which section is public before you lay out a towel.

### Quieter Coves on the Kabal Peninsula
The smaller bays on the Stari Grad bay can be reached by car along the Kabal peninsula. You can also rent a boat in town or book a taxi boat to the cove of your choice. These coves have few or no facilities. Bring water and food.

## Beachfront Apartments in Stari Grad

True beachfront apartments are rare in Stari Grad. The old town sits on a harbour used by ferries and yachts, not on a swimming beach. Most apartments advertised as "near the beach" are 300 m to 1 km from the water. The harbour views and the sea ladders on the quay are not the same as a beach.

### Old Town Apartments (Walk to Banj and Lanterna)
Staying in the old town puts restaurants, shops and the harbour at your door. Banj and Lanterna are both reachable on foot. Expect to pay roughly €70-€130 per night for a one-bedroom apartment in July and August. Prices fall noticeably in May, June and September. Rooms in the old town can be noisy on summer nights, so ask about street-facing windows.

### Maslinica Area (Closest to Sand)
Maslinica has the shortest walk to a sandy beach. The Maslina Resort is the high-end option on the bay. Hotel Antica is a seafront hotel with a pool, about 20 minutes on foot from the centre and close to Maslinica. Apartments in the surrounding residential area start from around €49 per night for budget units such as Apartments Ivanković. Higher-end units go above €120. The trade-off is distance from the centre. A car, bike or scooter is more useful here than in town.

### Near Lanterna
Apartmani Zlatarić is on the southern shore near Lanterna. It is about 1 km from the centre and about 800 m from Tvrdalj Castle. It suits guests who prefer swimming from rock platforms to walking into town.

## Where to Stay: Quick Guide
- **Best for first-time visitors:** old town, with Banj and Lanterna on foot.
- **Best for families with toddlers:** north side near Banj or the Maslinica area.
- **Best for sunsets and swimming off platforms:** south shore near Lanterna.
- **Best for a quiet base:** residential streets 10-20 minutes' walk from the harbour.

## Local Tips
- Banj has the calmest water. Lanterna has the better swimming depth off the platforms.
- Shoes with a grip help on the rock platforms and in the pebble coves. Sea urchins are common.
- The ferry from Split arrives at the harbour about 2 km from the centre, close to Maslinica. If your apartment is in the old town, plan a short taxi or a 25-minute walk with luggage.
- Maslinica and Lanterna are busy in July and August. Go before 10:00 or after 17:00.

## Honest Take
The sandy-beach claim for Maslinica is oversold. The sand is mixed with fine pebbles, and with almost no shade it gets hot by midday. It is still the best option on this part of Hvar for small children, but plan around the sun. Also, a "sea view" listing in Stari Grad usually means a view of the harbour or the town rooftops. If swimming matters most, book by walking distance to Banj or Lanterna, not by view.

## Beaches Beyond Stari Grad
Zavala, on the south coast of Hvar, is about 12 km away. Hvar Town is about 22 km. A rental car or scooter gives access to more secluded beaches, but Stari Grad's own beaches are enough for most stays of 3-7 days.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Stari Grad, Croatia?
faq.answer: Banj is the best for young children because it is calm, shallow and step-free. Lanterna is the best for sunsets and swimming off rock platforms. Maslinica is the best for sand.

faq.question: Does Stari Grad have a sandy beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Maslinica Bay, 2 km from the centre, has a sandy beach and is one of the few on Hvar. It has little natural shade, so bring an umbrella.

faq.question: Can you walk to the beaches from Stari Grad old town?
faq.answer: Yes. Banj is about 500 m away and Lanterna about 800 m, roughly a 15-minute walk along the waterfront promenade. Maslinica is 2 km away and reachable on foot or by bike along a coastal path.

faq.question: Are there true beachfront apartments in Stari Grad?
faq.answer: They are limited. Most apartments are 300 m to 1 km from the sea, and the closest options to a beach are in the Maslinica area. Check the distance to the water before booking.

faq.question: How much do apartments in Stari Grad cost?
faq.answer: Budget apartments start from about €49 per night. One-bedroom apartments in the old town usually cost €70-€130 per night in July and August. Prices fall in late spring and September.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Stari Grad free?
faq.answer: Yes, entry to Banj, Lanterna and Maslinica is free. Sunbed hire is charged separately where it is available.

quickAnswer: The best beaches in Stari Grad are Banj (pebbles, 500 m from the centre, good for children), Lanterna (rock platforms and pebbles, 800 m, best at sunset) and Maslinica (rare sand, 2 km). Most apartments are a short walk from the water. True beachfront stays are limited, and mostly around Maslinica.
